false_friends: South Australia (similar dry scrub/dirt terrain in remote areas)

road_furniture.km_marker_style: Yellow sign posts are the single strongest Western Australia-specific tell, distinct from the rest of the country. Utility poles here (and in Victoria) sometimes carry a distinctive 'mountain-shaped' support bracket.

architecture.roof_style: Single-story suburban houses in and around Perth, similar to the national default.
architecture.wall_construction: Brick veneer suburban housing around Perth on the sandy Swan Coastal Plain; isolated mining-town and roadhouse construction across the vast, sparsely populated remainder of the state.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Pale coastal tones around Perth; sun-faded dusty tones in the remote interior/Pilbara mining region.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Perth's coastal suburban sprawl on sandy, dune-backed terrain; remote mining infrastructure in the Pilbara/Kalgoorlie region; isolated roadhouses along the vast, empty Eyre Highway toward South Australia.

nature.vegetation: Sandy coastal plain vegetation and wetlands around Perth; increasingly sparse, reddish-orange-dirt desert scrub moving inland and north into the Pilbara and toward the Northern Territory border; unique and highly diverse wildflower regions in the southwest.
nature.terrain: An enormous, sparsely populated state — Perth and the fertile Swan Coastal Plain in the southwest corner, vast red-dirt desert and the Nullarbor Plain's dead-flat, treeless expanse further east toward South Australia.
nature.climate_signature: Mediterranean climate around Perth; hot, dry desert further inland and north — the slightly reddish-orange dirt tone is a recognized WA-specific clue distinct from the Red Centre's more saturated orange.

vehicles.plate_color: Western Australia plates are blue/white — one of the more reliable state-plate-colour tells (shared visually with Victoria/Tasmania, but geography narrows it further).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavy-duty mining and 4WD vehicles common given the Pilbara mining industry and vast remote distances.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Good coverage around Perth; sparse and patchy across the vast remainder of the state.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Perth is well covered; enormous gaps across the remote Pilbara, Kimberley and Nullarbor regions.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Both feature vast, sparsely populated red-dirt desert terrain
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Western Australia's yellow signposts are a specific state tell absent in the Northern Territory/Central Australia; WA's dirt tone trends more reddish-orange rather than the Red Centre's deeper saturated orange, though this is a subtle distinction best combined with pole/signage details.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Western Australia is far more sparsely populated overall with yellow signposts and long empty highways; the East Coast is denser, greener and far more developed.
